Please check file existence and permissions."` - These map directly to the scenarios in the story (missing file, wrong extension, invalid/unsafe path, filesystem error) and are exercised in tests.
2) Supporting utilities for path resolution, security, caching, and project boundaries - File: src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - JSDoc ties directly to story 006.0 and its requirements. - REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION: - `buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` builds candidate absolute paths: - Explicit relative paths (`./` or `../`) are resolved against `cwd` only. - Bare paths are resolved under `cwd` and each configured `storyDirectories` entry. - REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE & REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION: - `fileExistStatusCache: Map` caches filesystem checks. - `checkSingleCandidate(...)` uses `fs.existsSync` + `fs.statSync`, caches results and distinguishes `"exists"`, `"missing"`, and `"fs-error"`. - `getStoryExistence(...)` aggregates across candidates, preferring the first `exists`, otherwise a representative `fs-error`, otherwise `missing`. - `storyExists(...)` wraps `getStoryExistence` returning a boolean, preserving legacy API while benefiting from caching and error handling. - `__resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests()` allows tests to safely clear the cache. - REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION & REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY: - `enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd)` checks that normalized candidate paths are within the normalized project root. - Additional helpers `isAbsolutePath`, `containsPathTraversal`, `isTraversalUnsafe`, `hasValidExtension`, `isUnsafeStoryPath` provide reusable security checks.
- File: src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - JSDoc annotated with story 006.0 and `REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY`, `REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION`, `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS`. - REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY: - `analyzeCandidateBoundaries(...)` and `handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...)` use `enforceProjectBoundary` to classify candidate paths and report `invalidPath` when all candidates are outside the project. - REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION: - `performSecurityValidations(...)`: - Rejects absolute paths as `invalidPath` when `allowAbsolute` is false. - For paths containing traversal-like patterns, resolves and ensures they remain under `cwd`, otherwise reports `invalidPath`.
